_what: Work programs on this computer are doing that Trillion should show while it runs, read by computer/report-progress.mjs (started beside the connection by harness/wake-sessions.mjs). Each row names the progress files a program writes (`files`, ~ is the home folder and * one folder name, which fills {folder}), how to read each into one report for the person's Trillion (POST /mcp/api/tell/progress, src/tell-the-person.mjs report), and the words: `key`, `title` and `body` fill {name} from `values` (a value is a path into the file, optionally split on `split` and the `pick`th part taken) and from {folder} and {computer}. `done` and `total` are paths to counts in `unit` (a list of paths is their sum, and a "*" step is every item of a list there); `state` maps the file's own state word to running, done or failed (a word not listed is left out of the report); a file whose `pid` path names a program that is no longer running reports failed with `stopped_words`, once the file has not changed for `stopped_after_seconds` (until then the program is taken to be starting again on the same work, so nothing is said). A `key` names the work, never one start of the program doing it, so a program started again keeps changing the same notice. `kind` picks the card's look, channels and address in records/tell-the-person.json. A file that already says its work ended, or whose program stopped, is reported only when its `updated` time is within `settled_within_minutes`, so old finished work is never announced again. A file is read every `every_seconds` and reported only when what it says changed, and running work again every `resend_running_seconds` so a long quiet stretch never reads as stopped. `chips` (and `chips_by_state`) are short facts the card shows instead of the body, each words with {name} values (a chip naming a value the file does not carry is left out) and an optional tone. `title_by_state` and `body_by_state` word the title and body for one of the file's own state words, and a value the file stops carrying (a finished copy names no file in flight) keeps what it said last. `actions` (at most two shown, those whose `when` lists the file's state word) are what the person can press on the card: `write` writes `value` (with `stamp` set to the time) to `file` beside the progress file, `remove` removes that file; it is the program's own control file, so nothing here knows what pause or stop means. A new program is a row here and nothing else.
